messages:
maya_support: Customer reports mid-stream disconnects while using SSE on Android when switching from company VPN to cellular. They see a partial response (stream ends after ~60% tokens) and the client shows a 499/timeout. Customer says it repros reliably when toggling VPN quickly during a long generation.

eli_oncall: thanks, can you paste the request metadata (model, region, sdk version) and a short repro sequence? also need a client-side snippet if possible.

maya_support: customer provided this: model=redwood-v2-large, region=us-west-2, sdk=js@2.4.1, connection type=Android WebView in-app browser, auth=api-key. repro steps they gave: 1) start a 30s stream generation 2) while streaming, toggle company VPN off -> phone switches to carrier 3) stream stops mid-chunk and client shows timeout. sometimes reconnect shows duplicate partial content.

sam_platform: can you ask for the exact curl-equivalent and the `last_event_id` behavior? we support incremental resume via last-event-id if client implements it.

maya_support: asked customer; they said client isn't sending last-event-id and their reconnect just opens a fresh SSE. they attached a short client log: 
```
[2024-06-10T12:02:34.123Z] SSE open, id=null
[2024-06-10T12:02:36.345Z] chunk: token 0..120
[2024-06-10T12:02:46.110Z] network change: vpn->cellular
[2024-06-10T12:02:46.220Z] socket closed (code ECONNRESET)
[2024-06-10T12:02:46.450Z] client timeout -> abort stream, no resume attempted
```

eli_oncall: looks like a plain TCP reset during the VPN handoff. A couple quick checks: 1) what's the proxy/edge in use? if there's an intermediate proxy (company VPN) it may drop long-lived connections on network change. 2) can we see server-side logs around thread_ts 1716301123? ask for the request-id if they have it.

maya_support: they provided request-id header: rreq-8f3b2a. forwarding logs now.

deploy-bot: Incident ticket created RINF-3214 for request-id rreq-8f3b2a (priority: P3).

sam_platform: got the logs. server shows: 
```
2024-06-10T12:02:46.217Z INF stream start req=rreq-8f3b2a model=redwood-v2-large client=android-webview region=us-west-2
2024-06-10T12:02:46.342Z DBG token_chunk idx=0 size=121
2024-06-10T12:02:46.218Z ERR write failed: write tcp: connection reset by peer
2024-06-10T12:02:46.219Z INF client disconnected during stream req=rreq-8f3b2a reason=ECONNRESET chunk_idx=1
2024-06-10T12:02:46.220Z INF attempt fallback: enqueue resume token for client=mobile/unknown
```

eli_oncall: interesting line: "attempt fallback: enqueue resume token" — that's our internal hint for resume points, but it only helps if the client reconnects and provides their last_event_id. Customer said they don't implement last_event_id. we should recommend a quick patch: client should preserve last_event_id from the last SSE event and send `Last-Event-ID` header on reconnect. If they can't change client, server-side workaround: enable short-lived buffering + send final chunk on reconnect via resumable session (but that's infra change).

maya_support: customer asked for mitigations they can do now without server changes.

eli_oncall: recommend these client-side mitigations: 1) implement `Last-Event-ID` on reconnect to resume from last acknowledged token id. 2) on Android WebView, set `setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs(false)`? (just checking common webview issues), but more relevant: increase socket keepalive and set SSE heartbeat ping every 10s so proxies see activity. 3) on abort, attempt immediate reconnect with exponential backoff and send last_event_id. 4) avoid toggling VPN during active long streams if possible (app UX hint).

sam_platform: also suggest switching to our resumable-chunk API for long-running generations (we have a chunked upload/resume variant for customers with flaky mobile networks). file a feature/opt-in request if they'd like to enable it for their org.

customer_ops: customer asked for a small reproable example for their Android team. maya_support posted a minimal JS repro they can adapt: 
```js
const evt = new EventSource(url, { withCredentials: true });
evt.onmessage = (e) => { lastId = e.lastEventId || lastId; appendChunk(e.data); };
evt.onerror = () => { // on network change WebView often gives ECONNRESET
  // close and try immediate reconnect
  evt.close();
  setTimeout(() => {
    const reconnect = new EventSource(url, { headers: { 'Last-Event-ID': lastId } });
  }, 500);
};
```

maya_support: customer tried immediate reconnect but said the server sometimes returns a full new generation (duplicate content) instead of resuming. they reported duplicate tokens shown to user.

eli_oncall: that means server didn't find an associated resume lease for that client id. resume leases are short (30s) by default; network flip may have exceeded that. we can 1) increase lease window for sessions coming from mobile orgs, or 2) ask customer to reconnect faster (within 10s) and ensure they send Last-Event-ID header. Also confirm the client preserves the last SSE id between reconnections.

sam_platform: follow-up debugging step for us: correlate rreq-8f3b2a with the resume-queue subsystem and check whether a resume lease created and expired. I've added logs to RINF-3214 for resume-lease lifecycle dump.

maya_support: customer accepted two action items: (A) update Android client to keep lastEventId and attempt immediate reconnect with Last-Event-ID header; (B) we will run a one-off extension of resume lease for their org to 60s and monitor for a week. they want repro validation steps.

eli_oncall: provide client validation steps: 1) enable verbose client debug logs, 2) start a 40s generation, 3) flip VPN within 3-7s after stream start, 4) reconnect within 5s sending Last-Event-ID; expected: server resumes and final tokens continue from last chunk, no duplicate beginning tokens. if you still see duplicates, capture server request-id and send to us.

maya_support: closing loop with customer: thanks — we scheduled a short window to enable extended lease for your org tonight 02:00 UTC and we'll follow up with the logs. Also shared the JS snippet and suggested Android WebView changes.

customer_ops: customer replied: "thanks, we'll patch the client and test. appreciate the fast turnaround. will confirm after testing." :thumbsup:

eli_oncall: adding a small engineering note: we should consider adding a mobile detection rule to auto-extend resume leases for connections that drop due to NAT/VPN changes. filing internal ticket INF-563 for product review.

sam_platform: noted, and adding to RINF-3214.

deploy-bot: RINF-3214 updated: resume-lease extension enabled for org=acme-inc for 2024-06-11T02:00:00Z -> 2024-06-18T02:00:00Z.

maya_support: I'll follow up with customer tomorrow for final validation and then close the thread.

eli_oncall: thanks everyone. tips for docs: add a short KB on mobile SSE best practices (Last-Event-ID, heartbeat pacing, reconnect jitter).
